items.description: The Oued Draa wetlands are an important ecosystem for migratory birds and local wildlife in southern Morocco.
The Sebou River basin is one of Morocco's most fertile agricultural regions, supporting diverse crops.
Midelt is known as Morocco's 'apple capital,' with extensive orchards benefiting from the Atlas Mountains climate.
Tiznit region combines traditional agriculture with argan oil production, contributing to local livelihoods.
The oases around Ouarzazate are famous for date cultivation, a vital part of the local economy and diet.
Merzouga is the gateway to the Erg Chebbi dunes, offering spectacular sand landscapes and camel treks.
Sebkha Tindouf is a vast salt lake in the Sahara desert, an important geological feature and bird habitat.
Sebkha Boughaba Lake is a protected wetland and a crucial stopover point for migratory birds near the Atlantic coast.
Bin el Ouidane Lake is a large reservoir in the Middle Atlas, popular for water sports and its scenic beauty.
The Oued Guir is a seasonal river flowing through arid landscapes, creating temporary oases in its course.
The Oued Noun river and its valley create a unique desert ecosystem, supporting specific flora and fauna.
Oued Eddahab is a dry riverbed in the Western Sahara, vital for the region's limited plant and animal life.
Oued Massa is a coastal river in southern Morocco, forming wetlands known for their birdwatching opportunities.
Cap Ghir is a prominent headland on the Atlantic coast north of Agadir, offering dramatic cliff views.
